title: Traffic Gating Heuristic Diary
content:
Notes to self / working diary for release gating heuristics and rapid decisions.

Context and intent:
- Written while pairing with Priya on the 1.4.0 inference runtime rollout. Goal is to capture heuristics I keep reaching for when we gate traffic, pin versions, and choose when to widen canaries. This is a personal journal (not final runbook) but should be readable by on-call or SRE backup.

High-level goals:
- Avoid unnecessary full rollback for small regressions; prefer traffic tapering and quick fixes where safe.
- Keep user-facing latency/availability within SLAs and surface quality regressions quickly.
- Make pin/fallback decisions deterministic and reversible.

Principles I keep returning to:
1) Observe before interrupting: wait two steady 1-min datapoints (not spikes) before evicting traffic.
2) Use cohorts: 1% internal -> 5% canary -> 25% stagger -> general. If any audible symptom in 1% -> pause and investigate.
3) Gradual pinning: pin client versions only after 3 full days of stable canary and a successful synthetic job run.
4) Prefer model-variant fallback over full rollback when quality dips but latency is okay.

Short checklist (quick scan on wake-up):
- Are dashboards green? latency p50/p95, error-rate, request success.
- Any new alerts in #prod-alerts? (if yes, read the alert body for affected route/model)
- Canary traffic health: CPU/GPU saturation logs for dedicated hosts.
- Recent deploys: who merged what in last 2 hours? (PR links in the incident slack thread)

Step-by-step canary ramp I used in last roll (notes):
- T0 (00:00): release to staging, run full integration and synthetic prompt suite.
- T+30m: internal 1% (dev and internal beta users) for 1 hour. Observability: internal SLOs + example prompt traces.
- T+1.5h: 5% canary to subset of customers (non-critical routes). Run evals against top-500 prompts.
- T+6h: 25% stagger across regions (US-East then US-West). If p95 < 450ms and errors < 0.1% additional -> continue.
- T+24h: 100% if no anomaly and key regressions pass.

Gating signals and thresholds I act on (subject to tuning):
- Latency: p95 increase > 30% relative to baseline over 10m window -> pause expansion.
- Errors: any 5xx spike > 0.5% absolute or sustained doubling of baseline -> hold and triage.
- Quality: BLEU/ROUGE-like automated metrics on eval set showing regression > 2% -> hold and run manual sample.
- Cost/throughput: GPU mem pressure > 85% for >5m -> throttle canary.
- New anomalies in trace errors (timeouts vs model failures) -> route to engineering triage.

Pinning and version rules (my shorthand):
- Pin = route-level config referencing exact model artifact hash (not tag).
- If a route has pin older than 7 days and a critical security fix exists, we must force pin update via SR change ticket.
- Hotfix policy: if we need to pin back to previous artifact, do it on the smallest scope possible (customer cohort / route) and annotate with JIRA and slack message.

Rollback playbook (quick):
1) Pause expansions and cut canary to 0% if systemic.
2) If issue confined to model variant, re-route affected traffic to fallback variant (same model family).
3) If runtime bug, pin to last-known-good artifact hash and notify on-call with reason.
4) Run targeted synthetic tests. If green, start staged re-expansion (50% for 1h then 100%).
5) Postmortem assignment within 48h for rollbacks that affect >1% customers or lasting >30m.

Monitoring snippets I check quickly (build into dashboard):
- route:token-generation p95, p50, errors
- gpu_utilization per-host
- model_latency_by_sequence_len
- canary_eval_quality_delta (daily automated job)

Quick CLI snippets (notes to self):
- Increase canary: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/rollouts -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}' -d '{"route":"/generate","percent":5,"artifact":"sha256:abcd..."}'
- Pin route: rwctl routes pin /generate --artifact sha256:abcd --reason "rollback after spike" --ticket JIRA-REL-312
- Snapshot logs for window: rwctl logs fetch --route /generate --since 2026-02-28T10:00:00Z --until 2026-02-28T10:20:00Z > /tmp/gcrash.log

Observations from last two experiments (free text):
- Priya's heuristic to hold at 5% for 3h instead of 1h caught a slow-rolling memory leak (good catch). Add as optional step in next runbook.
- We still lack cheap A/B tools to test prompt-distribution regressions quickly. A daily lightweight sampling job could help.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide whether 1% internal should include select enterprise customers who accept early traffic (we currently exclude them). Pros/cons to document.
- Add automated annotation linking PRs to rollout IDs (manual today).
- Draft a short 'rollback rationale' template for SR/onsite engineers to fill when pinning.

Final quick mental checklist before widening:
- Confirm at least 2 engineers watching (Slack thread + Zoom optional).
- Confirm alert routing and escalation steps are up to date in incident PS.
- Confirm synthetic job run last 30m passed.

End of diary entry. This file is a working mental model — will refine into a formal runbook once we stabilize heuristics and get sign-off from SRE.

---
Footnotes: keep the language plain; this is my internal decision trail. If you copy sections into an official runbook, remove the ‘notes to self’ fragments and expand the escalation steps with names and phone numbers.
